Two substantive corrections were made rather than inherited:

- The previous comment in parity_expectations.tsv labelled the 1414/2000
architecture divergence "the parity ceiling". It is not. COMPARISON_SEMANTICS
requires oracle and native to run in the same process, build, and target, and
RunIdentity.requireSameBuild() enforces it, so both sides of every differential
comparison share an architecture and that axis is not observable to the runner.
Accepting the lenient reading would have demoted 70.7% of the adversarial
corpus to the invariant tier permanently.

- This bead's own premise figure (739 units / ~15 bond lengths, from the r05
standalone C++ review probe) is superseded by the manifest: the same single
member measures 0.580 bond lengths (29 units), 25x smaller. Recorded in
PARITY_MANIFEST.md where the claim is made. The correction strengthens the
strict position, and it is why the invariant/statistical tier is left
unpopulated: 0.580 bond lengths sits inside a tolerant band, so adversarial/1695
is held to a tolerant comparison against the published bound rather than excused
to statistics.

Closed in 3c9eb9a. Demonstrated end to end: with a failure planted in a fuzz target, tools/run-fuzz exited 1 and named the target while the underlying zig build fuzz --fuzz=3000 for the same plant exited 0. No gate in the tree reads that exit status - the only other --fuzz consumer, tools/check-fuzz-seed-promotion, is also output-based. Pinned rather than verified once: tools/run-fuzz --self-test asserts both crashing shapes are detected from real captured OUTPUT, a clean FUZZING REPORT is not mistaken for a crash, and the --fuzz call does not consult returncode; proven to have teeth against two planted violations, and required by check-gate-strength so deleting it fails the build. REFINEMENT worth carrying: the original claim 'a crashing fuzz run exits 0' was too broad. A target failing on the INITIAL smoke input exits 1; only a crash the fuzzer had to DISCOVER exits 0. So the exit status is right for failures nobody needed a fuzzer for and wrong for exactly the ones it exists to find - meaning a spot-check with a trivially-failing target would show it working.

Closed in bd215d4. performance-check is a real gate: tests/oracle_benchmark.zig times native and oracle in one process on the same members in the same build/target/optimize mode, and the same binary with --enforce compares each bucket's ratio against conformance/performance_thresholds.tsv. Thresholds set from four measured runs with headroom, provenance recorded in the file. Verified to have teeth against two planted violations (raised coverage floor, lowered ratio). Two findings matter more than the numbers: native cannot lay out ANY member of the medium/large/huge buckets, so the gate covers 36 of 100 benchmark members - now ratcheted via min_compared_members so it cannot shrink silently; and native is at parity on the tiny median while ~10-14x the oracle at the tiny p95 in every run, filed as cgz-twy. A member native refuses is skipped on BOTH sides so the ratio stays like-for-like. check-gate-strength now requires --enforce and the embedded thresholds in place of the removed addFail.

Landed in 579f663 (PR #31). All five buckets carry measured thresholds and min_compared_members=20, so the gate covers 100 of 100 benchmark members instead of 36. Every edit was a tightening or a first-time value; no decision bead needed. tiny p95 dropped 20.00 to 6.00. The one correction worth carrying: a first attempt used 25 percent headroom and set small median to 2.40 against an observed 1.683-1.798; the next run measured 2.409 and the gate went red on machine load alone, and a later run measured 2.614. That was reverted and the margin is now about 40 percent over the highest of sixteen samples. Verified green on four consecutive local runs plus both CI platforms, and teeth proven with three planted violations covering the median ceiling, p95 ceiling and coverage floor separately. Residual risk recorded in the file: small p95 at 4.30 sits only about 15 percent above an observed 3.739, the tightest margin present, left alone because raising it would need a decision bead.

Recovered on 2026-08-29. The schema cursor is back at v53, bd runs with no BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW override, and the events table is re-tracked with audit-event versioning restored. Verified by SQL rather than by absence of an error: schema_migrations holds 53 rows with max version 53, and the issue count was unchanged across the operation. The binary needed no change; 1.2.2 was already the newest release in both homebrew-core and upstream, and is the fix for the accidental 1.2.1 rather than a successor to it. Two things worth knowing for next time. First, the merge with origin/main reintroduced the skew mid-merge, jumping the cursor to v66, because the remote still carried the migrated schema; the stray row was removed before the merge was concluded, so the corrected cursor is now pushed and the remote reads v53 too. Second, upstream's re-track command stages the events table but not dolt_ignore itself, leaving the working set dirty; that was committed separately. bd_events_journal and bd_events_seq remain ignored, since upstream's guide names only events.

Decided 2026-08-29. small max_p95_ratio raised 4.30 to 5.60, and performance-check enforced on both CI platforms. 5.60 is about 24 percent over the highest of eight CI samples, the headroom every other row carries. Rationale recorded in conformance/performance_thresholds.tsv with the eight samples: the old 4.30 came from four quiet runs on one host observing 3.457-3.483, and CI's own logs showed the real spread is 2.917 to 4.525 across both platforms, so the threshold sat inside the range of what it measures. This is not admitting a regression; native did not get slower, the same code measures 2.917 on one runner and 4.525 on another. The second question raised here, whether a p95 ratio is a sound observable at all, was deliberately deferred rather than decided, so cgz-7v2.4.10 and cgz-7v2.4.11 could proceed; it is cgz-7v2.4.15.
